tasks.title: Correct the Result<T>.Value documentation to describe default(T), not null (MASTER-044 / CORE-005, measurement.md section 3 fact 1)
acceptance: A1. The XML summary of the Value property in src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs no longer claims the property is null when the operation failed. Falsifiable by: grep -c "when the operation failed" src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs -- returns 0. PREDICATE VALIDATED by the architect at 42ec7e9 in C:/dm-wt/6b-xii: this phrase matches exactly one line, :27, which is the Value summary (the case that MUST match), and does NOT match the two near-misses at :32 and :37, which read "when the operation succeeded" and document Error and ErrorCategory -- both of which are genuinely nullable (string? and Nullable<ErrorCategory>) and must be left alone. So this command cannot be satisfied by deleting the wrong summary. NOT satisfied at startRef: the command returns 1 there.

A2. The Value summary states that a failed result carries the DEFAULT of T rather than null, written as <see langword="default"/>. That markup form is the closest precedent this repository has -- src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/MutationOutcomeExtensionsTests.cs:126 uses <see langword="default"/> in exactly this sense. Counted by the architect at 42ec7e9: grep -rn 'langword="default"' --include=*.cs src/ (with /obj/ and /bin/ filtered) returns n = 1. ONE INSTANCE. The repository has done this once; this is cited as the nearest precedent, NOT as a convention. Falsifiable by: grep -c 'langword="default"' src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs -- returns at least 1. NOT satisfied at startRef: it returns 0 there.

A3. The Value documentation names the consequence for the only closed construction production uses -- that for Result<Guid> the failure default is Guid.Empty, which is indistinguishable from a Guid a successful operation could in principle return. The closure figure is re-measurable without git: grep -rn ": ICommand<Guid>;" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Application | grep -v "/obj/" | wc -l returns 4, and grep -rhno "Result<[A-Za-z0-9_?<>, .]*>" over the four production projects shows Result<Guid> as the only closed construction, everything else being Result<T> / Result<TResult> plumbing (both re-run by the architect at 42ec7e9). Falsifiable by: the text printed by sed -n '/public bool IsFailure/,/public T? Value/p' src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs contains the string Guid.Empty. NOT satisfied at startRef: that range is lines 23-29 there and contains no such string.

A4. The Value documentation names IsSuccess/IsFailure as the only failure signal and says in terms that the default value must not be read as one. This is the half of CORE-005's stated remedy that the sentinel in T2 exists because of -- "stop callers from treating the default as a failure signal" (docs/audit/01-domain-application.md, CORE-005 Suggested direction). Falsifiable by: the text printed by sed -n '/public bool IsFailure/,/public T? Value/p' src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs contains the string IsFailure inside the Value summary or its remarks, on a line beginning with ///. NOT satisfied at startRef: the only IsFailure in that range is the property declaration at :23, not a /// line.

A5. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design -- this task changes documentation only and the public surface must not move. The Value declaration is still exactly "public T? Value { get; private init; }" and T remains unconstrained. Falsifiable by: grep -c "public T? Value { get; private init; }" src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs returns 1, AND grep -c "where T" src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs returns 0. Rationale recorded so a later reader does not re-open it: T? on an unconstrained T is the CORRECT C# annotation for "may be the default"; the defect CORE-005 found is the prose, not the annotation, and adding a struct or notnull constraint would narrow a type nothing asks to be narrowed.

A6. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design: src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs is CRLF throughout and ends with a final newline, matching .editorconfig:8-9. Falsifiable by: python -c "import sys;b=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read();print(b.count(b'
')==b.count(b'
'), b.endswith(b'
'))" src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs -- prints True True. The Edit tool emits LF and this file is CRLF, so an edit can mix them. grep -c $'$', cat -A and git show <rev>:<path> all lie about line endings in this environment and are not acceptable substitutes.

A7. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design -- the base tree already builds clean, and this asserts a documentation-only change does not break that. dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.Application/DungeonMaster.Application.csproj -c Debug exits 0, its MSBuild summary reports "0 Warning(s)" and "0 Error(s)", and grep -cE "(warning|error) [A-Z]+[0-9]+" over the captured output returns 0. NOTE ON THE COMMAND: the plain grep -icE "warning|error" form used elsewhere in this project is correct over dotnet test output but is UNSATISFIABLE over dotnet build, because MSBuild always prints the literal lines "0 Warning(s)" and "0 Error(s)" even on a clean build, so that form returns 2. This criterion is live rather than a formality for a doc-only change: a malformed <see cref="..."/> raises CS1574, and Directory.Build.props:5 sets TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, so it fails the build.

A8. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj reports Failed: 0 and exits 0. Baseline re-measured by the architect at 42ec7e9 in C:/dm-wt/6b-xii with dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln -v q --nologo: DungeonMaster.Tests 850 passed / 0 failed, DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests 23 / 0, DungeonMaster.App.Tests 102 / 0, process exit code 0.

tasks.title: Remove the unreachable success-path Guid.Empty sentinel from MapCanvasViewModel (MASTER-044 / CORE-005, measurement.md section 3 fact 3)
acceptance: B1. src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs contains no comparison of a dispatch result's Value against Guid.Empty. Falsifiable by: grep -n "Value == Guid.Empty" src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs -- prints nothing and exits 1. PREDICATE VALIDATED by the architect at 42ec7e9: it matches exactly one line, :213, "if (addResult.Value == Guid.Empty)" (the case that MUST match), and does NOT match the near-miss at :222, "addResult.Value,", which is a bare read passed as the area identifier to UpdateAreaOutlineCommand and must survive. NOT satisfied at startRef: the command prints :213 there. Why the sentinel goes rather than gets fixed: it sits AFTER the addResult.IsFailure early return at :206-211, so it can only ever be reached on the success path; on that path AddAreaCommandHandler yields area.Id (src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/AddArea/AddAreaCommandHandler.cs:33) and Entity.Id is initialised to Guid.NewGuid() (src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs:11), so the branch is unreachable in practice -- and what it does if reached is return silently with no error reported to the user, which is worse than the failure it was standing in for.

B2. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design, and load-bearing: the AddAreaCommand dispatch's failure branch survives. Falsifiable by: grep -c "addResult.IsFailure" src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs returns 1. src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/FailureIsSurfacedTests.cs scans this file from disk and requires every captured dispatch to be followed by a "{name}.IsFailure" branch before the next dispatch or the end of the member (its private IsBranchedOn helper). The IsFailure branch at :206 precedes the sentinel, so removing the sentinel does not disturb it -- but this criterion pins that.

B3. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design, and load-bearing: the failure is still routed to the composition root's single error channel. Falsifiable by: grep -c "context.ReportFailure(addResult)" src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs returns 1. FailureIsSurfacedTests.EveryViewModelWithADispatch_DeclaresAnErrorMessageProperty requires this file's count of "context.ReportFailure(" to be at least its count of "dispatcher.SendAsync", so dropping a routing site reddens that fact even though the IsFailure branch around it survives.

B4. The area identifier produced by the successful AddAreaCommand is still passed to UpdateAreaOutlineCommand, and is now the file's only read of that result's Value. Falsifiable by: grep -c "addResult.Value" src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs returns exactly 1, and grep -n "addResult.Value" on the same file prints a line inside the "new UpdateAreaOutlineCommand(" argument list. NOT satisfied at startRef: the count is 2 there (:213 and :222). This criterion and B1 are deliberately separate -- B1 says the sentinel went, this says the legitimate read stayed.

B5. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design: src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs is CRLF throughout and ends with a final newline, matching .editorconfig:8-9. Falsifiable by: python -c "import sys;b=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read();print(b.count(b'
')==b.count(b'
'), b.endswith(b'
'))" src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs -- prints True True. grep -c $'$', cat -A and git show <rev>:<path> all lie about line endings here.

B6. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design: dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.App/DungeonMaster.App.csproj -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 -c Debug exits 0, its MSBuild summary reports "0 Warning(s)" and "0 Error(s)", and grep -cE "(warning|error) [A-Z]+[0-9]+" over the captured output returns 0. Do not substitute the plain grep -icE "warning|error" form: it is correct over dotnet test output but ALWAYS returns 2 over dotnet build, because MSBuild prints "0 Warning(s)" and "0 Error(s)" literally even on a clean build. Close any running DungeonMaster.App before building, or MSB3026/MSB3027. .editorconfig:64 sets IDE0055 to severity = warning and Directory.Build.props:5/:16 set TreatWarningsAsErrors=true with EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true, so a stray blank line or a wrong indent fails this command; the file is tab-indented.

B7. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design, and the empirical guard on B2 and B3: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln -v q --nologo reports Failed: 0 on all three test-project lines and exits 0, with DungeonMaster.Tests reporting 850 passed. Baseline re-measured by the architect at 42ec7e9 in C:/dm-wt/6b-xii with that exact command: 850 / 23 / 102, total 975 passed, 0 failed, process exit code 0. This is the criterion that catches a source-scanning fact disturbed by the edit -- FailureIsSurfacedTests additionally asserts a hard Be(14) on the dispatch count across the four dungeon-detail view models, and that test lives in DungeonMaster.Tests.

tasks.title: Repair the test whose name denies what it asserts, and pin the sentinel's absence (MASTER-044 / CORE-005, measurement.md section 3 facts 3 and 4)
acceptance: C1. No test method name in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Results/ResultOfTTests.cs claims a failed Result<Guid> carries no value. Falsifiable by: grep -n "CarriesNoValue" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Results/ResultOfTTests.cs -- prints nothing and exits 1. NOT satisfied at startRef: it prints :36, Failure_WithCategory_IsNotSuccessAndCarriesNoValue, whose own assertion at :46 is result.Value.Should().Be(Guid.Empty). This encodes disciplines/test.md, Naming: "The name must not claim more than the test checks. A name broader than its assertions misleads every later reader."

C2. No XML summary in that file claims a failed result carries no value. Falsifiable by: grep -in "no value" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Results/ResultOfTTests.cs -- prints nothing and exits 1. NOT satisfied at startRef: it prints :33, "Verifies that a failed result carries the supplied message and category and no value." Separate from C1 because the name and the summary are two separate false statements about the same test and either can be fixed without the other.

C3. That file contains a [Fact] whose name states that a failed result carries the DEFAULT value, and whose body asserts that the failed Result<Guid>'s Value equals default(Guid) written literally as default(Guid) rather than as Guid.Empty -- so the assertion says what it means rather than naming a constant that happens to have the same bits. Falsifiable by: grep -n "public void Failure_" on the file prints a method whose name contains Default, AND grep -c "default(Guid)" on the file returns at least 1, AND dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ResultOfTTests" reports Failed: 0. NOT satisfied at startRef: grep -c "default(Guid)" returns 0 there.

C4. The XML summary of that [Fact] states that the default is NOT a failure signal and that IsSuccess/IsFailure is. Falsifiable by: grep -B 8 -n "public void Failure_" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Results/ResultOfTTests.cs -- the printed block contains IsFailure (or IsSuccess) on a line beginning with ///. NOT satisfied at startRef: the summary block above that method, :32-35, mentions neither.

C5. NEW FILE src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs declares a public test class in namespace DungeonMaster.Tests.App.ViewModels containing a [Fact] that reads the four dungeon-detail view-model sources -- DungeonDetailViewModel.cs, DungeonHeaderViewModel.cs, FloorListViewModel.cs, MapCanvasViewModel.cs -- from disk through DungeonMaster.Tests.App.Theme.RepoPaths, and fails if any of them compares a dispatch result's .Value against Guid.Empty or default. The four names are listed explicitly rather than globbed, following src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/FailureIsSurfacedTests.cs:27-33, whose comment gives the reason: the fact must fail loudly if one of them is renamed or removed, not quietly scan whatever it happens to find. Source-scanning through RepoPaths is this repository's established mechanism for pinning a source-level fact: grep -rln "RepoPaths" --include=*.cs src/ | grep -v "/obj/" returns 20 paths at 42ec7e9, of which 19 are under src/DungeonMaster.Tests (18 consumers plus RepoPaths.cs itself) and one is src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests/UiTestEnvironment.cs, which is outside src/DungeonMaster.sln by design and must not be added to it. n = 18 consumers -- this is a convention. The file is tab-indented; .editorconfig:64 sets IDE0055 to severity = warning and Directory.Build.props:5/:16 make that fail the build. Falsifiable by: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests" reports Failed: 0 and at least 1 passed.

C6. The detector is a predicate over text, reachable from the test without touching the filesystem, and the same file asserts that it FLAGS the constructed must-match case -- the exact sentinel form this session removed, the string "if (addResult.Value == Guid.Empty)". Exercising a scanning predicate against constructed input rather than only against the real checkout is the mechanism src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/RepoPathsTests.cs:13-17 states the reason for. This encodes disciplines/test.md, Coverage: "A test is shown able to fail -- seen failing before it is made to pass, or shown to catch the defect it exists for when that defect is injected." Falsifiable by: grep -c 'addResult.Value == Guid.Empty' src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs returns at least 1, and the filtered dotnet test run in C5 reports Failed: 0.

C7. NEAR-MISS 1, asserted NOT flagged: the bare read "addResult.Value," -- a result value passed as an argument with no comparison. This one is not hypothetical: src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs still contains exactly that line after T2 (see B4), so a predicate that flagged it would fail the C5 fact against the fixed tree. Falsifiable by: the constructed string appears in ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs inside an assertion that the predicate returns no finding for it, and the filtered dotnet test run in C5 reports Failed: 0.

C8. NEAR-MISS 2, asserted NOT flagged: a Guid.Empty comparison on something that is not a result value -- the string "if (_dungeonId != Guid.Empty)". Also not hypothetical: src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/DungeonDetailViewModel.cs:133 is that line verbatim, and :117 assigns _dungeonId = Guid.Empty. A predicate that scanned for Guid.Empty alone would flag both and the C5 fact could never pass. Falsifiable by: the constructed string appears in ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs inside an assertion that the predicate returns no finding for it, and the filtered dotnet test run in C5 reports Failed: 0.

C9. NEAR-MISS 3, asserted NOT flagged: a line containing .Value only as a substring of an unrelated identifier -- the string "using DungeonMaster.Domain.ValueObjects;". src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/MapCanvasViewModel.cs:12 is that line verbatim, and it is why a naive .Value substring search over these files returns three hits rather than two. Falsifiable by: the constructed string appears in ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs inside an assertion that the predicate returns no finding for it, and the filtered dotnet test run in C5 reports Failed: 0.

C10. The scan is guarded against vacuity: the C5 fact asserts it actually read four sources before asserting anything about their contents. src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/RepoPaths.cs:52-55 states the reason in its own words -- the helper "returns an EMPTY LIST when the pattern matches nothing. It does not throw and it does not assert: non-emptiness is the caller's guard, so that a vacuous scan fails against the fact that depended on it". Falsifiable by: grep -n "HaveCount(4)\|NotBeEmpty()" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs prints at least one line, and the filtered dotnet test run in C5 reports Failed: 0.

C11. PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design for the edited file and asserted for the new one: both src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Results/ResultOfTTests.cs and src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/ResultSentinelIsAbsentTests.cs are CRLF throughout and end with a final newline, matching .editorconfig:8-9. Falsifiable by, for each file: python -c "import sys;b=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read();print(b.count(b'
')==b.count(b'
'), b.endswith(b'
'))" <file> -- prints True True. The Write tool emits LF, so a newly written file is LF unless converted; four consecutive new .cs files across three prior sessions were caught only by counting in binary. grep -c $'$', cat -A and git show <rev>:<path> all lie about line endings here.

C12. MIXED CRITERION -- its no-regression clause is satisfied at startRef by design, its count clause is NOT, and it is deliberately not labelled a preserve criterion for that reason: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln -v q --nologo reports Failed: 0 on all three test-project lines and exits 0, and DungeonMaster.Tests reports strictly MORE than 850 passed. Baseline re-measured by the architect at 42ec7e9 in C:/dm-wt/6b-xii with that exact command: DungeonMaster.Tests 850 / 0, DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests 23 / 0, DungeonMaster.App.Tests 102 / 0, total 975 passed, process exit code 0. Strictly more, not a fixed target: C3 renames an existing fact rather than adding one, while C5 to C10 add several, and the exact number is the implementer's to report rather than the architect's to guess. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE, pre-freeze consistency check: the architect labelled this "PRESERVE CRITERION, satisfied at startRef by design". The first clause is; the second is not -- DungeonMaster.Tests reports exactly 850 at startRef, so "strictly more than 850" fails there, which is correct and is the point. The label was the error, not the criterion. It mattered because a preserve label exempts a criterion from the vacuity check, and this one neither needed nor deserved that exemption.
